issues.legal_issue: An annual municipal property-tax assessment list must be authenticated before the official year for which the tax is levied ends.
material_facts: The municipality prepared and published an assessment list for an official year, invited objections, and made changes following decisions on those objections.
The municipality authenticated the finalized assessment list after the official year had ended.
The tax sought under the list was an annual tax for that official year.
issues.conclusion: The assessment list was void and inoperative for levying the tax, and it did not create liability to pay tax under the revised rates.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 78 to 84 of the Bombay Municipal Boroughs Act, 1925, read as a whole, authentication completes the assessment and levy process. Because the tax is annual and for a particular official year, authentication must occur during that year. Section 84 assumes an authenticated list is available for adoption for the following year, while section 82 supports the requirement that changes taking effect for an official year be made during that year. The Court also relied on the consistent interpretation of the Act by the Bombay, Karnataka, and Gujarat High Courts, including Sholapur Municipality v. Governor General and Sholapur Municipal Corporation v. Ramchandra, and on the legislative recognition of that interpretation in section 84A, added by Bombay Act 53 of 1954. The Court applied the principle that a statute must be read as a whole and that long-standing interpretations of a State statute should not ordinarily be disturbed where the legislature has left them undisturbed.

predicates.annual_municipal_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns a municipal tax assessed annually for a particular official year.
predicates.levy_completed_by_authentication: The municipality's assessment process makes authentication of the finalized assessment list the step that completes the levy and creates liability to pay.
predicates.authentication_after_tax_year: The municipality authenticated the assessment list only after the official year for which the tax was levied had ended.

issues.definition: When a municipal annual-tax assessment is completed by authenticating its finalized list, authentication after the relevant official year means the list is inoperative and creates no liability to pay the tax.

issues.legal_issue: A short statutory limitation period for a suit against a municipality begins when the cause of action accrues, and a challenge to a void assessment list accrues when the municipality seeks to recover tax under it.
material_facts: The municipality authenticated the assessment list after the official year had ended, making the list void and inoperative.
The rate-payers sued to challenge recovery of tax under that list and sought relief including a declaration and repayment of excess tax collected.
The municipality argued that the cause of action arose when the list was authenticated.
The record did not establish when demands for payment were issued or when particular rate-payers paid the tax.
issues.conclusion: The cause of action did not arise merely when the void list was authenticated; it arose when the municipality sought to recover tax under it. Because the municipality did not establish when the relevant demands or payments occurred, it did not establish that the suit was time-barred, and its limitation defense failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 206A of the Bombay Municipal Boroughs Act, 1925, bars a suit against a municipality concerning an act done in execution or intended execution of the Act unless it is commenced within six months after the cause of action accrues. A rate-payer may ignore a void and inoperative assessment list as a nullity; the cause of action to challenge it accrues when the municipality seeks recovery under it. Without evidence showing when the recovery demand was made or the tax was paid, the municipality cannot establish that the limitation period expired before the suit was filed.

predicates.municipal_tax_recovery_suit: The proceeding is a suit by rate-payers against a municipality concerning recovery of municipal tax.
predicates.recovery_sought_under_void_assessment: The municipality sought to recover tax from rate-payers under an assessment list that was void and inoperative.
predicates.demand_or_payment_timing_unproved: The evidence does not establish when the municipality demanded payment or when the rate-payers paid the tax.

issues.definition: In a rate-payer suit challenging recovery under a void assessment, if the timing of the recovery demand or payment is unproved, the municipality has not established that the suit is barred by limitation.
